Caszual TV Time Windows development bundle

1. Put the Caszual TV Time JAR in your Minecraft mods folder.
2. Start Minecraft. The Windows capture helper is bundled inside
   the JAR and is extracted automatically to:
   config/caszual_tv_time/native/caszual-tv-time-capture.exe
3. /caszual_tv_time_capture windows
4. /caszual_tv_time_capture start <windowIndex> <channel>
5. Look at a connected TV wall and run:
   /caszual_tv_time_capture tune <channel>

Current real-window development stream:
- AUTO video codec prefers H.264 (JCodec baseline)
- automatic fallback to delta-Deflate
- periodic keyframes + packet-loss recovery
- bounded media fragmentation/reassembly
- selected-process Opus audio (48 kHz stereo)
- automatic raw PCM fallback
- positional mono TV/speaker playback

Capture quality controls:
/caszual_tv_time_capture quality LOW
  192x108 @ 12 FPS
/caszual_tv_time_capture quality BALANCED
  320x180 @ 15 FPS (default)
/caszual_tv_time_capture quality HIGH
  640x360 @ 20 FPS

Codec controls:
/caszual_tv_time_capture codec AUTO
/caszual_tv_time_capture codec H264
/caszual_tv_time_capture codec DELTA

AUTO is the recommended test mode.

Speaker test:
1. Place a Caszual TV Time Speaker block.
2. Look directly at it.
3. Run:
   /caszual_tv_time_test speaker <channel> <role> [volume] [range]

Roles:
FULL, LEFT, RIGHT, CENTER, REAR_LEFT, REAR_RIGHT, LFE

LEFT/REAR_LEFT use the captured left stereo channel.
RIGHT/REAR_RIGHT use the captured right stereo channel.
FULL/CENTER/LFE currently downmix both channels to mono.

/caszual_tv_time_capture status shows current FPS, combined kbps,
active video codec, audio codec, quality profile, and video compression ratio.

This build validates the full capture -> compression -> server
relay -> remote connected-TV video + multi-speaker positional
audio path with H.264 + Opus enabled by default, while both retain
safe fallback paths for troubleshooting.
